items.review_rationale: Read the finite standard-open covering data, all module localizations, agreement after localizing to pairwise overlaps, and the asserted characterization by diagonal localization. Kept the gluing conclusion separate from the definition of compatibility.

references.phrase: module localization M_{f_i} and M_{f_i f_j}

references.context: Commutative algebra: ideal (f_1,…,f_n)=R, ensuring associated principal standard opens cover Spec(R)
Zariski basic open consisting of primes not containing f_i; pairs intersect as D(f_i f_j)

references.phrase: tuple of locally defined module sections m_i
references.context: Element m_i of each localization M_{f_i}, viewed over the corresponding standard open

references.phrase: restriction from M_{f_i} to M_{f_i f_j}
references.context: Further module localization along f_j, used to compare local values on a common overlap
Map sending m to its images m/1 in each local module; its image is the compatible-tuples subgroup

references.phrase: such tuples are exactly the image of M
references.disposition: Finite principal-open descent/gluing statement under the unit-ideal hypothesis; not an assertion for arbitrary noncovering families.

items.review_rationale: Read locally defined modules on finitely many standard opens and the pairwise localized isomorphisms with identity and triple-cocycle constraints. Distinguished module descent from the separate scheme gluing datum.

references.phrase: Spec(R) with its prime spectrum topology
finite standard open cover by D(f_i)
references.context: Finite principal Zariski opens whose union is Spec(R), equivalently the f_i generate the unit ideal
R_{f_i f_j}-linear isomorphisms between the two localized overlap modules
Compositions of pairwise transition isomorphisms agree with the direct transition over every triple common localization

references.disposition: Descent coherence conditions on overlap isomorphisms; not simply arbitrary pairwise module isomorphisms.

items.review_rationale: Read nonemptiness and undirected zigzag connectivity of any two objects through finitely many morphisms in a category. Did not require a single forward arrow, invertibility of arrows, or topological connectedness.

references.phrase: finite zigzag of arrows between objects
references.context: A finite sequence of consecutive objects with a morphism joining each pair in either direction; arrows need not be invertible

references.disposition: The nonemptiness requirement is explicit; an empty category is not connected under this convention.

references.phrase: directions of zigzag arrows may alternate
references.disposition: Connectivity uses the underlying undirected incidence of morphisms, not a directed path condition.

items.review_rationale: Read the qualification that the indexing category, not a limiting object, is connected. Examined both limits and colimits of diagrams and retained their separate generic existing meanings.

references.context: Functor from the connected indexing category into a target category whose limit or colimit is considered

references.disposition: The adjective describes the shape/index of a limiting construction; it is not a connected topological object or a claim that the limit object is connected.
